import pytest

class TestIsValidEmailHappyPath:
    """Standard well-formed emails should return True."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email", [
        "simple@example.com",
        "very.common@example.com",
        "disposable.style.with+symbol@example.com",
        "other.email-with-hyphen@example.com",
        "user.name+tag+sorting@example.com",
        "x@example.com",                          # minimum local part
        "a@b.cc",                                 # minimum domain + 2-char TLD
        "example-indeed@strange-example.com",
        "user123@test-domain.co.uk",              # subdomain
        "UPPERCASE@DOMAIN.COM",                   # uppercase allowed
        "user@123numericdomain.com",              # numeric domain labels allowed
    ])
    def test_valid_emails(self, email):
        assert is_valid_email(email) is True


class TestIsValidEmailInvalidFormat:
    """Malformed emails missing required components should return False."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("email", [
        "",                           # empty string
        "plainaddress",               # no @ symbol
        "@nodomain.com",              # no local part
        "missingdomain@",             # no domain/TLD
        "missingtld@domain",          # no dot + TLD
        "missingdot@domaincom",       # dot in TLD missing
        "two@@at-signs.com",          # multiple @ symbols
        "user@domain@domain.com",     # multiple @ symbols variant
        "user name@domain.com",       # space in local part
        "user@dom ain.com",           # space in domain
        " leading@space.com",         # leading whitespace
        "trailing@space.com ",        # trailing whitespace
        "user@domain.c",              # TLD only 1 char
        "user@domain.1",              # TLD numeric single char
        "user@domain.123",            # TLD numeric multi char
        "user@domain.c0m",            # TLD alphanumeric (contains number)
        "user@domain.com.",           # trailing dot after TLD
    ])
    def test_invalid_emails(self, email):
        assert is_valid_email(email) is False


class TestIsValidEmailEdgeCases:
    """
    Boundary values and quirks specific to this regex implementation.
    
    The pattern `[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+` for the domain is very permissive:
    dots and hyphens are allowed in positions that stricter validators
    might reject (e.g., consecutive dots, leading dots, or adjacent
    hyphens).
    """

    def test_tld_boundary_exactly_two_chars(self):
        assert is_valid_email("user@domain.uk") is True

    def test_tld_boundary_one_char_is_invalid(self):
        assert is_valid_email("user@domain.u") is False

    def test_unicode_in_local_part_rejected(self):
        assert is_valid_email("üsér@domain.com") is False

    def test_unicode_in_domain_rejected(self):
        assert is_valid_email("user@domäin.com") is False

    def test_domain_starting_with_dot_is_valid_per_regex(self):
        # Quirk: dot is included in the domain character class
        assert is_valid_email("user@.domain.com") is True

    def test_consecutive_dots_in_domain_are_valid_per_regex(self):
        # Quirk: regex does not prevent consecutive dots
        assert is_valid_email("user@domain..com") is True

    def test_hyphen_at_domain_boundaries_is_valid_per_regex(self):
        # Quirk: hyphen allowed immediately after @ or before the TLD dot
        assert is_valid_email("user@-domain.com") is True
        assert is_valid_email("user@domain-.com") is True

    def test_trailing_newline_is_considered_valid(self):
        """
        Python's re.match with `$` matches just before a trailing newline,
        so this returns True. This test documents that behavior.
        """
        assert is_valid_email("user@domain.com\n") is True

    def test_carriage_return_newline_is_invalid(self):
        # \r before \n prevents $ from matching correctly
        assert is_valid_email("user@domain.com\r\n") is False


class TestIsValidEmailErrorCases:
    """Non-string inputs should raise TypeError from `re.match`."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_input", [
        None,
        123,
        12.34,
        [],
        {},
        set(),
        object(),
    ])
    def test_non_string_input_raises_type_error(self, bad_input):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            is_valid_email(bad_input)
